title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier‑Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared‑Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study (study‑cnd‑2026‑001) to test whether a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increases oracle pass rates for LLM‑produced network configurations on vendor‑diverse intent→configuration tasks. The frozen design used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (one generator call per pair consumed by both conditions), declared model gpt‑5‑mini, a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a repair budget ≤1 call/task. The run produced 200 complete pairs (400 episodes), model_calls_used=200, baseline = 200/200 oracle passes, guarded = 200/200 oracle passes; absolute paired difference = 0.00 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00], bootstrap_resamples=10000, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p=1.00. The null result is design‑bound: every shared candidate passed the deterministic oracle, so the repair stage was never exercised. We release the audited artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and SHA‑256 digests) and provide artifact‑grounded recommendations for informative follow‑ups (independent generation semantics, calibrated difficulty, larger repair budgets, validator stress tests).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are being explored as intent→configuration agents for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness (safety, reachability, vendor idiom compliance) is essential, yet LLMs can produce plausible but unsafe configurations. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→repair: a generator proposes a candidate, a deterministic validator (oracle) checks objective properties, and, if failed, a repair module attempts corrective generation. Prior work reports gains from verifier guidance or repair with counterexamples, but rigorous preregistered, artifact‑anchored comparisons are rare. We preregistered study‑cnd‑2026‑001 to provide a confirmatory, fully archived measurement of whether verifier assistance increases oracle pass rates. The preregistration fixed generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), model, validator, repair budget, stratified task bank, and an analysis executor; all artifacts and per‑file SHA‑256 digests are archived (see execution/execution_manifest.json and provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 1872df1e...). Our principal finding: under the frozen shared_initial_candidate semantics the repair stage was never invoked because every shared candidate passed the deterministic oracle, producing identical pass rates in both conditions. We report the run, deterministic reconciliation, and precise artifact‑grounded guidance for follow‑ups that permit repairs to act.
sections.related_work: Recent NetOps work studies intent translation, configuration synthesis, verifier/constraint augmentation, and repair workflows. Representative artifacts in our evidence bundle motivated the study: MeshAgent (constraint guidance), NetConfEval (intent→configuration benchmarks), and verifier‑grounded program repair examples (StruSpec). Those works support verifier‑assisted architectures and informed our preregistered design choices. Unlike many prior studies, we preregistered the estimand and generation semantics, executed the run autonomously, and archived every raw and derived artifact with SHA‑256 digests to permit reproducible audit (execution/* and analysis/*). The supplied literature artifacts are listed in cited_record_ids and were used for literature positioning only; all empirical claims below are drawn from the archived execution and analysis artifacts of study‑cnd‑2026‑001.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design. The experiment was preregistered as study‑cnd‑2026‑001 (preregistration SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2). The preregistration froze: primary_estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one generator call per pair consumed by both conditions); declared_model = gpt‑5‑mini; validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; paired design with Npairs=200. The statistical analysis was fixed: paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test. All files and per‑file SHA‑256 digests are archived (execution/execution_manifest.json; analysis/*).

Task bank and stratification. The preregistered task bank contained 200 pairs stratified by protocol and vendor: four protocol buckets (BGP/OSPF/ACL/VLAN = 50 pairs each) with per‑protocol vendor allocation Cisco=17, Juniper=17, Arista=16 (total Cisco=68, Juniper=68, Arista=64). Complexity was split: simple=100, complex=100. Each task entry in execution/task_manifest.jsonl includes intent text, initial and expected final states, required_sequence, constraints, and a reference answer (representative entries are archived; see execution/scoring/task‑000001‑baseline.json). The manifest records deterministic generation seeds used by the autonomous generator.

Generator, adapter, and generation semantics. The declared generator was gpt‑5‑mini via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model configuration and adapter metadata are archived in execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 1acce92558ed...). The frozen shared_initial_candidate semantics produced a single generator call per pair; that single candidate was supplied unchanged to both baseline (unconstrained) and guarded (verifier‑assisted) scorers. This choice minimizes generator calls but couples the two conditions by design and is the proximate cause the repair stage never fired in this run. The execution manifest records model_calls_used=200 and per‑call provider traces in execution/provider_calls/.

Validator and repair. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses candidate configurations, simulates changes on an emulated deterministic network model, and returns a detailed validator trace including normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, final_state, violation list, and repair_applied boolean. Repair was permitted per preregistration but invoked only when validator failures occurred; in this run repair_applied=false for every archived validator trace and repair calls invoked=0. All validator traces and scoring JSON files are archived under execution/scoring/ with SHA‑256 digests.
sections.results:
Execution and scoring artifacts. Execution completed as preregistered: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200 (one shared generation per pair). Analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 1cb072b4...) reports baseline_success_count = 200/200 (100%), guarded_success_count = 200/200 (100%). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...) is n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0.

Confirmatory inference (artifact: analysis/results.json). The paired estimate (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) = 0.00; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00] (bootstrap_resamples=10000, seed=1729). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. These numbers are extracted from the analysis executor output and the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 940b48e7...).

Representative validator evidence. Representative per‑pair scoring artifacts show the deterministic validator trace, normalized configuration, parsed command counts, final simulated device state, and repair_applied=false. Example: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 eaf96aec...) contains the normalized_configuration and validator validation_after/final_state dictionaries confirming the candidate satisfied all oracle predicates. Similar paired artifacts exist across the full 200‑pair set; each is hashed in the execution manifest for audit.

Deterministic reconciliation and accounting. analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA‑256 799b23b9...) confirms accounting consistency: complete_pair_count=200; baseline_from_contingency=200; guarded_from_contingency=200; hosted_model_call_event_count=200; cache_hit_count=0; cache_miss_count=200; all deterministic consistency checks passed. The reconciliation artifact and per‑file SHA‑256 digests allow external reproducible verification that raw responses, provider traces, and scoring records are mutually consistent.
sections.discussion:
Design interpretation: the observed null effect is a direct consequence of the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics. With a single generator call per pair, both conditions consumed identical generated artifacts; because each shared candidate passed the deterministic validator in every case, repairs were never invoked (repair_calls_invoked=0). Thus the run answers the preregistered estimand under the frozen design but cannot adjudicate whether repair loops would help when initial candidates fail. This is an expected statistical ceiling: without any discordant pairs (n10=n01=0), the paired difference is deterministically zero and the bootstrap CI collapses to [0,0]. The archival artifacts support this causal chain (see execution/execution_manifest.json and all execution/scoring/*.json entries).

Operational lessons and artifact‑grounded next steps. The archive permits two concrete, low‑risk experimental variants that will let repair mechanisms be exercised while preserving reproducibility: (1) independent generation semantics — generate one candidate per condition per pair (expected model_calls ≈ 400) so baseline/guarded may receive distinct candidates and repairs can be triggered when guarded invokes repair; (2) calibrated/harder task slices — add or replace a fraction of the task bank with higher‑difficulty intents or boundary conditions (requires only manifest edits and reseeding) so initial candidates fail deterministically and repair paths are used. Both variants can be executed with the same validator and adapter; per‑file hashing and the established provenance pipeline will produce an auditable run comparable to the current bundle.

Threats to validity (artifact‑anchored). Internal validity — the frozen generation semantics and the single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) determined outcomes; prompt sensitivity remains a key internal threat and is recorded per provider trace. Construct validity — the deterministic validator enforces objective emulation predicates; oracle blind spots remain possible and are flagged in validator traces as oracle_coverage diagnostics. External validity — synthetic/emulated tasks and single model limit generalization. Conclusion validity — paired design and preregistered analysis were followed exactly; the degenerate contingency is an honest inferential outcome of the frozen design.

Reproducibility instructions (artifact pointers). All artifacts needed to reproduce or extend the run are archived and hashed. Key entries: master prompt provenance provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e...), preregistration SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b1b..., model configuration execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 1acce925...), execution manifest execution/execution_manifest.json, per‑pair raw responses execution/responses/*.txt, provider traces execution/provider_calls/*.json, validator traces execution/scoring/*.json, analysis artifacts analysis/*.csv and analysis/results.json. To implement independent generation semantics, update the preregistration generation_semantics to independent_per_condition, adjust planned model_calls, and rerun via the same adapter; the framework will archive the new provider calls and validator traces for audit.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed an audited paired emulation test of verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Both baseline and guarded achieved 200/200 oracle passes; repairs were never invoked; paired difference=0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p=1.00). The null outcome is design‑bound: shared initial generation plus the specific task bank and generator behavior produced a ceiling that prevented repair invocation. The run demonstrates the importance of matching generation semantics and task difficulty to the scientific estimand: to measure repair effectiveness the pipeline must allow generator variance and oracle failures. We publish the full audited artifact bundle and provide concrete artifact‑grounded recommendations (independent generation, calibrated difficulty, larger repair budgets, validator stress tests) that can be executed reproducibly using the archived prompts and manifests.

limitations: Confirmatory conclusions apply only to the exact preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, single declared model gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, synthetic/emulated task bank of 200).

Shared_initial_candidate execution semantics created a ceiling effect: because the single shared generated candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle for every task, the guarded repair stage was never invoked (repair calls invoked = 0), preventing measurable guarded benefit in this run.
Emulation with a deterministic validator and synthetic tasks does not capture full production heterogeneity (real vendor images, runtime nondeterminism, device‑specific quirks).
Single‑model execution limits generality across model families and instruction‑tuning variants.
Repair budget was intentionally limited (≤1 call/task) by preregistration; richer iterative repair policies remain unexplored in this run.
Oracle blind spots (uncovered semantic failure modes) remain possible; oracle‑coverage diagnostics are archived in validator traces and should be examined when extending the task bank.
